land.text: 'much of modern central and eastern Henan' (Li Mi page), without the Sui-held city of Luoyang

predecessors.note: The rebels near Luoyang coalesced under Li Mi in 616 (Transition page); Zhai Rang offered him the title Duke of Wei in spring 617 (Li Mi page).

land.text: 'much of modern central and eastern Henan' (Li Mi page), without the Sui-held city of Luoyang

successors.note: Wang Shichong, commanding for Yang Tong's Luoyang regime, crushed Li Mi at Yanshi in October 618; that regime became Wang Shichong's Zheng in 619. Li Mi fled to the Tang, submitted to Emperor Gaozu in winter 618 and died on 20 January 619.

capitals.name: Jinyong (near Luoyang)
capitals.note: The page names no capital; 'in spring 618 Li moved his headquarters' to Jinyong, a fortress near Luoyang. Coordinates are the researcher's approximation.

rulers.name: Li Mi
rulers.note: Duke of Wei, 617-618 (infobox); the title was first offered by Zhai Rang.

correction.text: 'much of modern central and eastern Henan' (Li Mi page), without the Sui-held city of Luoyang

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 617-618 for a state Cliopatria lacks: 'much of modern central and eastern Henan came under Li's rule' (table 'Eastern Henan', 617-618). The page gives no area; Luoyang stayed Sui until Wang Shichong's coup.

region.text: 'much of modern central and eastern Henan' (Li Mi page), without the Sui-held city of Luoyang

ledger.note: 617: Li Mi becomes Duke of Wei. After the Luokou victory in spring 617 Zhai Rang 'offered the title of Duke of Wei' to Li Mi (infobox 617-618); the Transition page has the rebels near Luoyang coalescing under him in 616.

region.text: the Sui eastern capital and its surroundings

ledger.note: 618: Li Mi tightens his grip on Luoyang. In spring 618 he 'seized Jinyong, a fortress near Luoyang' and moved his headquarters there, 'trying to put a strangle hold on Luoyang'; 'I have not yet captured the eastern capital.'

region.text: the Sui eastern capital and its surroundings

ledger.note: 618: Wang Shichong crushes him. 'Wang Shichong crushed his forces at Yanshi' (October 618; 'Wang took this opportunity to launch a major attack on Li in fall 618', Wang Shichong page); Li fled west to the Tang.

region.text: 'much of modern central and eastern Henan' (Li Mi page), without the Sui-held city of Luoyang

ledger.note: 618: Li Mi's Wei ends at Yanshi. He submitted to Emperor Gaozu in winter 618 and was killed on 20 January 619 'when he tried to reestablish his own independence' (Transition page).

wars.name: Wang Shichong's campaign against Li Mi
wars.outcome: Wang Shichong, for Yang Tong's regime, beat Li Mi at Yanshi in October 618 and Li fled to the Tang.
wars.note: A summer 618 peace between Wang and Li preceded it.

certainty.note: The page gives a province span (central and eastern Henan), no boundary.

sources.title: Li Mi (Sui dynasty)
sources.note: Duke of Wei 617, Jinyong spring 618, Yanshi October 618, death 20 January 619, Henan.

sources.note: Fall 618 attack on Li Mi at Yanshi.

sources.title: Transition from Sui to Tang
sources.note: The Wei in the list of rival regimes; Li Mi 'made Duke of Wei' in the rebels' coalescing of 616.

notes: REBEL STATE for a Sui rival Cliopatria lacks. The Transition page dates the coalescing to 616 and the Li Mi page the Duke of Wei title to spring 617 (infobox 617-618); the dossier starts in 617. The Sui dossier's loss (617) and gain (618) name this slug. The region is the page's province span with Luoyang cut out; Dou Jiande 'sent Li a submission' in 618 (Dou Jiande page) but nothing says Dou's land was Li's.
